messages:
nina: Quick sync  We need one concise artifact that ties together tenancy lanes, multi-region fallback, and explicit canary gates for PI planning. Focus: predictable QoS for customers + operational safety. Can owners land a draft by Wed?

ash: Agreed. My ask: make the policy executable. Minimal primitives: lane_id, residency_constraints, fallback_chain, model_variant_constraints, quality_budget. Keep the runtime evaluation deterministic.

mika: Customer input: three lanes we should support out of the gate: Dedicated (pinned pools + SLA), Affinity (prefer local region but allow fallback), Economy (shared infra, quantized models ok). Need clear contract sentences for each.

pete: Ops must see a checklist-before-canary: per-tenant telemetry present, eviction-sentinel configured, warmup window configured to pre-warm KV caches, and autoscale policies validated on a dry-run. If missing, block. :no_entry:

anil: Prioritization heuristic idea: build a 2D map (business_value vs ops_risk) and then a short-run roadmap for Q2. I'll prototype a short scoring sheet.

nina: Owners: Ash -> policy spec + sample YAML, Pete -> pre-canary gating checklists + runbooks, Mika -> customer mapping + contract wording, Anil -> prioritization sheet. Oli/Taylor - will you own slides?

ash: Sample policy snippet (toy):
```
lane: "affinity"
residency: "prefer: us-west-2; hard_block: none"
fallback_chain: ["shared-eu", "shared-global"]
model_variant: { allow_quant: true, prefer_f16: false }
quality_budget_pct: 4
rollout: ["ff_canary", "small_ramp", "auto_ramp"]
```
Runtime must be able to evaluate "model_variant" boolean checks and map to a compatible model artifact.

pete: I'll add: pre-canary automated probes include: per-tenant p50/p95/p99; eviction-sentinel rate; kv_cache_hit_rate; cold-start-latency. Gate rule: if any probe missing or stale > 2m -> block canary. Also add an emergency-evict playbook: if eviction_rate > 0.25% for 15m -> failover sessions to next fallback and notify SRE.

mika: Sample contract lines inserted into the doc: "Affinity lane: best effort region preference; no contractual residency guarantee. Dedicated lane: contractual region residency and 99.9% regional uptime SLA." I'll attach 3 anonymized customer quotes.

anil: I'll weight business_value x2 in the prioritization sheet and add an 'ops_mitigation_cost' factor so we don't undercount risky items.

oli: A couple of infra notes: cross-region fallback will temporarily inflate p99 due to cache refill and model loading. Suggest ramping with warmup windows and a staggered traffic shift (10% -> 30% -> 60%). Also add a sanity metric: quality_delta_pct measured on a holdout eval set.

ash: Good point. Add policy field: warmup_window_seconds and traffic_shift_schedule. Example: warmup: 600, schedule: [10,30,60,100]. Also add a field 'quality_guard' referencing an eval_suite id.

nina: Deploy-bot - can you scaffold the repo doc and create a tracking branch so owners can PR?

deploy-bot: created doc https://redwood.internal/docs/tenant-routing-hyperscale-checkin and branch routing/hyperscale-3712345000

pete: I'll write the minimal runbook and include test commands (curl examples + a simple k6 script snippet) in the doc.

anil: Sending the prioritization sheet in chat after this thread. Will include 6 sample asks.

mika: Please ensure billing tags are included per-lane so we can surface cost deltas to customers. Also include rate-limit buckets per lane to protect shared infra.

nina: Great. Please add your sections by Tues EOD. We'll use the scoring sheet at PI planning to decide Q2 scope. Meeting Thurs 10am to review draft. Thanks all! :rocket:
